revealWordProblem.title: Apply: Street Corn Recipe
revealWordProblem.text: Eduardo is going to make 30 ears of grilled Mexican street corn for a party using the recipe shown. He has all the ingredients except Cotija cheese. Eduardo tells a friend he will buy four 10-ounce packages of cheese that each contains 2 cups. How would you respond to Eduardo?
revealWordProblem.imageAlt: A recipe card for Grilled Mexican Street Corn listing the ingredients for 6 ears of corn.
revealWordProblem.sampleAnswer: The recipe serves 6 ears and calls for 1/2 cup of Cotija cheese, so the scale factor for 30 ears is 30 ÷ 6 = 5. Eduardo needs 5 × 1/2 cup = 2 1/2 cups of cheese. Four 10-ounce packages at 2 cups each give 4 × 2 = 8 cups — more than three times what he needs. I'd tell Eduardo he's buying way too much cheese: 2 packages (4 cups) would already cover his 2 1/2 cups, so buying four packages wastes cheese and money.

questions.stem: A ratio table shows (2, 6), (4, 12), and (6, 18). Which ordered pair comes next if the pattern continues?
questions.explanation: The pattern adds 2 to x and 6 to y each time. After (6, 18): x = 6+2 = 8, y = 18+6 = 24. The next point is (8, 24).
choiceFeedback: Not quite. The pattern adds 2 to x and 6 to y each time.
Your x-value follows the pattern, but y only moved up 4. Look at how much y grows from one row to the next.
This jumps two steps in x while y only takes one. Each row moves x and y forward together, so check the step size for both.
hints: Watch each coordinate separately: x goes 2, 4, 6, … and y goes 6, 12, 18, …
Find the jump in the x-values and the jump in the y-values, then apply both jumps to (6, 18).
The x-values climb by 2, so add 2 to the 6 first. Then find the y-jump from 6 → 12 → 18 and add it to 18.
questions.stemEs: Una tabla de razones muestra (2, 6), (4, 12) y (6, 18). ¿Cuál par ordenado sigue si el patrón continúa?
questions.explanationEs: El patrón suma 2 a x y 6 a y cada vez. Después de (6, 18): x = 6+2 = 8, y = 18+6 = 24. El siguiente punto es (8, 24).
hintsEs: Observa cada coordenada por separado: x va 2, 4, 6, … y y va 6, 12, 18, …
Halla el salto de los valores de x y el salto de los valores de y, y luego aplica ambos saltos a (6, 18).
Los valores de x suben de 2 en 2, así que suma 2 al 6 primero. Luego halla el salto de y de 6 → 12 → 18 y súmalo a 18.

questions.stem: When you graph equivalent ratios, the points will always form what shape?
choices: A straight line through the origin
questions.explanation: Equivalent ratios are proportional, so their graph is always a straight line that passes through the origin (0, 0).
choiceFeedback: Re-check how many times you need to multiply or scale.
A zigzag would mean the ratio changes from point to point. Equivalent ratios grow by the same step every time, so the points stay in line.
A circle would bring the points back to where they started. Equivalent ratios keep climbing in one direction as x increases.
hints: Think about what happened when you plotted equivalent-ratio points earlier in this lesson.
Equivalent ratios grow steadily: every time x rises by the same amount, y rises by the same amount. What shape is steady growth?
Picture plotting (1, 2), (2, 4), (3, 6) and connecting them — and check whether (0, 0) would fit the pattern too.
questions.stemEs: Cuando graficas razones equivalentes, ¿qué forma tomarán siempre los puntos?
questions.explanationEs: Las razones equivalentes son proporcionales, así que su gráfica siempre es una línea recta que pasa por el origen (0, 0).
choicesEs: Una línea recta que pasa por el origen
hintsEs: Piensa en lo que pasó cuando graficaste puntos de razones equivalentes antes en esta lección.
Las razones equivalentes crecen de manera pareja: cada vez que x sube lo mismo, y sube lo mismo. ¿Qué forma tiene un crecimiento parejo?
Imagina graficar (1, 2), (2, 4), (3, 6) y unirlos, y revisa si (0, 0) también encajaría en el patrón.

questions.stem: A ratio table shows (2, 8), (3, 12), and (5, 20). What is the y-value when x = 7?
questions.explanation: The ratio is y/x = 8/2 = 4. For every x, y = 4x. When x = 7: y = 4 × 7 = 28.
choiceFeedback: Not quite. The ratio is y/x = 8/2 = ___.
It looks like you added instead of scaling. In a ratio table y is a multiple of x, so find y ÷ x from a row you already have.
That multiplies by 5, but check the given rows: 8 ÷ 2 and 12 ÷ 3 both give the same number, and it is not 5.
hints: Compare each pair: 2 → 8, 3 → 12, 5 → 20. What is done to x to get y every time?
Find the multiplier by dividing y by x for any pair — it should be the same for all three. Then apply it to x = 7.
Divide 8 ÷ 2 to find the rule's multiplier. Then multiply 7 by that number.
questions.stemEs: Una tabla de razones muestra (2, 8), (3, 12) y (5, 20). ¿Cuál es el valor de y cuando x = 7?
questions.explanationEs: La razón es y/x = 8/2 = 4. Para cada x, y = 4x. Cuando x = 7: y = 4 × 7 = 28.
hintsEs: Compara cada pareja: 2 → 8, 3 → 12, 5 → 20. ¿Qué se le hace a x para obtener y cada vez?
Halla el multiplicador dividiendo y entre x en cualquier pareja: debe ser el mismo en las tres. Luego aplícalo a x = 7.
Divide 8 ÷ 2 para hallar el multiplicador de la regla. Luego multiplica 7 por ese número.

2. Plot the points on the coordinate plane
3. Proportional Relationship: Points form a straight line passing through the origin (0, 0)
reviewHighlights.watchOut: A common mistake in Graph Ratio Tables is writing the ordered pair in the wrong order — putting the second table value first instead of matching (x, y) to the table's column order. For example, if a recipe table shows 2 cups of sugar for every 4 cups of flour, a student might plot (4, 2) instead of (2, 4), landing the point in a completely different spot on the grid. Before you plot, check: which quantity goes on the x-axis, and does your ordered pair start with that number?

level1.stem: Which point would NOT be on the graph of the ratio 1:5?
level1.explanation: For the ratio 1:5, every y-value should be 5 times the x-value. (3, 10): 5 × 3 = 15, not 10. So (3, 10) does not belong.
choiceFeedback: Re-check how many times you need to multiply or scale.
Test it: 4 × 5 = 20, so this pair does follow the ratio 1:5. Keep hunting for the pair that fails the test.
Test it: 5 × 5 = 25, so this pair fits the rule 1:5. The odd one out is the pair where y is not 5 times x.
hints: On the 1:5 graph, every y-value is exactly 5 times its x-value.
Test each point: multiply its x by 5 and see whether you land on its y. You're hunting for the one that misses.
Work through the points in order, multiplying each x by 5. The one whose y does not match is the answer.
level1.stemEs: ¿Cuál punto NO estaría en la gráfica de la razón 1:5?
level1.explanationEs: Para la razón 1:5, cada valor de y debe ser 5 veces el valor de x. En (3, 10): 5 × 3 = 15, no 10. Por eso (3, 10) no pertenece.
hintsEs: En la gráfica de 1:5, cada valor de y es exactamente 5 veces su valor de x.
Prueba cada punto: multiplica su x por 5 y ve si llegas a su y. Buscas el que no cuadra.
Empieza con (3, 10): multiplica 3 × 5 y compara tu resultado con 10. Prueba los demás puntos igual.

level1.stem: (Lesson 3.1) A recipe uses 4 cups of milk and 1 cup of cream. What is the ratio of milk to cream?
level1.explanation: A ratio compares quantities in the order given. Milk to cream = 4 to 1, or 4:1.
choiceFeedback: The order matters — what is named first should be first in the ratio.
You added the numbers together — a ratio compares two amounts, not their sum.
5 is the total number of cups, not the amount of cream. This compares the whole recipe to one part instead of milk to cream.
hints: Re-read the question: it asks for milk to cream, in that exact order.
In a ratio, the amount named first goes first. Find the milk amount and the cream amount before you write anything.
Underline the two amounts: milk = 4 cups, cream = 1 cup. Write them in the same order the question names them.
level1.stemEs: Una receta usa 4 tazas de leche y 1 taza de crema. ¿Cuál es la razón de leche a crema?
level1.explanationEs: Una razón compara cantidades en el orden que se indica. Leche a crema = 4 a 1, o 4:1.
hintsEs: Vuelve a leer la pregunta: pide leche a crema, exactamente en ese orden.
En una razón, la cantidad que se nombra primero va primero. Halla la cantidad de leche y la de crema antes de escribir nada.
Subraya las dos cantidades: leche = 4 tazas, crema = 1 taza. Escríbelas en el mismo orden en que las nombra la pregunta.

level1.stem: (Lesson 3.1) Chef Reyes uses 6 strawberries and 2 bananas in a smoothie. What is the part-to-whole ratio of bananas to total fruit?
level1.explanation: Total fruit = 6 + 2 = 8. The part-to-whole ratio of bananas to total fruit is 2:8.
choiceFeedback: Re-check: does this show a part being compared to the whole group?
This compares bananas to strawberries, which is part-to-part. A part-to-whole ratio needs the total number of pieces of fruit as the second number.
The order matters — what is named first should be first in the ratio.
hints: Notice the word 'total' — this is a part-to-WHOLE ratio, not banana-to-strawberry.
First find the total fruit by adding strawberries and bananas. Then compare bananas to that total.
Add 6 + 2 to get the total fruit. Then write the bananas' number first, followed by that total.
level1.stemEs: El chef Reyes usa 6 fresas y 2 plátanos en un batido. ¿Cuál es la razón parte a todo de plátanos a fruta total?
level1.explanationEs: Fruta total = 6 + 2 = 8. La razón parte a todo de plátanos a fruta total es 2:8.
hintsEs: Fíjate en la palabra 'total': esta es una razón parte a TODO, no de plátano a fresa.
Primero halla la fruta total sumando las fresas y los plátanos. Luego compara los plátanos con ese total.
Suma 6 + 2 para obtener la fruta total. Luego escribe primero el número de plátanos, seguido de ese total.

level1.stem: (Lesson 3.3) A recipe uses 3 eggs for every 5 cups of flour. How many eggs are needed for 15 cups of flour?
level1.explanation: The scale factor is 15 ÷ 5 = 3. Multiply the eggs by 3: 3 × 3 = 9 eggs.
choiceFeedback: Re-check how many times you need to multiply or scale.
10 doesn't come from scaling the egg row. Find the factor with 15 ÷ 5 and apply it to the 3, not the 5.
It looks like you multiplied by 4 instead of 3. Check the factor: 15 ÷ 5 tells you how many times the table grows.
hints: Notice the flour jumped from 5 cups to 15 cups — the eggs must grow by the same factor.
Find the scale factor by dividing the new flour by the recipe's flour, then multiply the eggs by that same factor.
Divide 15 ÷ 5 to get the scale factor. Then multiply 3 eggs by that factor to scale the recipe.
level1.stemEs: Una receta usa 3 huevos por cada 5 tazas de harina. ¿Cuántos huevos se necesitan para 15 tazas de harina?
level1.explanationEs: El factor de escala es 15 ÷ 5 = 3. Multiplica los huevos por 3: 3 × 3 = 9 huevos.
hintsEs: Fíjate que la harina pasó de 5 tazas a 15 tazas: los huevos deben crecer con el mismo factor.
Halla el factor de escala dividiendo la harina nueva entre la harina de la receta y luego multiplica los huevos por ese mismo factor.
Divide 15 ÷ 5 para obtener el factor de escala. Luego multiplica los 3 huevos por ese factor para escalar la receta.

level1.stem: (Lesson 3.3) Which row does NOT belong in a ratio table for 4:5?
level1.explanation: 6:10 simplifies to 3:5, not 4:5. The other ratios (8:10, 12:15, 16:20) all simplify to 4:5.
choiceFeedback: 8:10 divides by 2 to give 4:5, so it DOES belong in the table. Simplify each row and hunt for the one that does not give 4:5.
You doubled it, but check if that's the right scale factor.
16:20 DOES belong in the table: dividing both numbers by 4 gives 4:5. Simplify each option and find the one that does not give 4:5.
hints: Every row in a 4:5 table must simplify back to exactly 4:5.
For each choice, ask: can I multiply 4 AND 5 by the same number to get these two values? Check both parts, not just one.
Work through the choices in order. For each one ask: is there a single number that multiplies BOTH 4 and 5 into these two values?
level1.stemEs: ¿Cuál fila NO pertenece a una tabla de razones de 4:5?
level1.explanationEs: 6:10 se simplifica a 3:5, no a 4:5. Las demás razones (8:10, 12:15, 16:20) se simplifican todas a 4:5.
hintsEs: Cada fila de una tabla 4:5 debe simplificarse exactamente a 4:5.
Para cada opción pregunta: ¿puedo multiplicar el 4 Y el 5 por el mismo número para obtener esos dos valores? Revisa ambas partes, no solo una.
Prueba la primera opción, 6:10: ¿por cuánto multiplicas el 4 para obtener 6? ¿Multiplicar el 5 por ese mismo número da 10?

level2.stem: Points from a ratio table are plotted at (1, 4), (2, 8), and (3, 12). What is the ratio of y to x for each point?
level2.explanation: For each point: 4÷1 = 4, 8÷2 = 4, 12÷3 = 4. The ratio of y to x is always 4:1.
choiceFeedback: That is what you get if you wrote the two quantities in the reverse order. Instead: The ratio of y to x is always 4:1 — the y-value divided by the x-value.
Those numbers do come from the table, but they are written x to y and left unsimplified. Divide y by x and reduce.
This mixes numbers from two different points. Pair each point's own y with its own x, then simplify.
hints: The question asks y to x — the up-value compared to the across-value, in that order.
Divide y by x for each point. Equivalent ratios should give the same result all three times.
Take (2, 8): divide 8 ÷ 2. Check that (1, 4) and (3, 12) give the same value, then write it as y first, x second.
level2.stemEs: Los puntos de una tabla de razones se grafican en (1, 4), (2, 8) y (3, 12). ¿Cuál es la razón de y a x en cada punto?
level2.explanationEs: Para cada punto: 4÷1 = 4, 8÷2 = 4, 12÷3 = 4. La razón de y a x siempre es 4:1.
hintsEs: La pregunta pide y a x: el valor vertical comparado con el horizontal, en ese orden.
Divide y entre x en cada punto. Las razones equivalentes deben dar el mismo resultado las tres veces.
Toma (2, 8): divide 8 ÷ 2. Comprueba que (1, 4) y (3, 12) den el mismo valor y luego escríbelo con y primero y x después.

level2.stem: Two students graph ratio tables. Student A plots (1,2), (2,4), (3,6). Student B plots (1,3), (2,6), (3,9). Whose line is steeper?
level2.explanation: Student A's ratio is 1:2 (y goes up 2 for each 1 in x). Student B's ratio is 1:3 (y goes up 3 for each 1 in x). A higher rate of change means a steeper line, so Student B's is steeper.
choiceFeedback: Not quite. Student A's ratio is 1:2 (y goes up 2 for each 1 in x).
Both lines do rise, but not at the same rate. Compare how far y climbs for each single step in x.
You actually have enough information — every point gives a unit rate. Divide y by x for one point in each set and compare the two.
hints: Steepness comes from how fast y climbs each time x grows by 1 — not from who has bigger points overall.
Find each student's rate: divide y by x for one of their points. The bigger rate makes the steeper line.
Student A's line rises 2 for each 1 in x (see (1, 2)). Find Student B's rise from (1, 3), then compare the two rates.
level2.stemEs: Dos estudiantes grafican tablas de razones. El estudiante A grafica (1,2), (2,4), (3,6). El estudiante B grafica (1,3), (2,6), (3,9). ¿Cuál línea es más inclinada?
level2.explanationEs: La razón del estudiante A es 1:2 (y sube 2 por cada 1 de x). La razón del estudiante B es 1:3 (y sube 3 por cada 1 de x). Una tasa de cambio mayor significa una línea más inclinada, así que la del estudiante B es más inclinada.
hintsEs: Lo empinado depende de qué tan rápido sube y cada vez que x crece 1, no de quién tiene los puntos más grandes en general.
Halla la razón de cada estudiante: divide y entre x en uno de sus puntos. La razón mayor da la recta más empinada.
La recta del Estudiante A sube 2 por cada 1 de x (mira (1, 2)). Halla la subida del Estudiante B con (1, 3) y compara las dos razones.

level2.stem: Recipe: 1 cup berries to 2 scoops yogurt. With cups on x and scoops on y, which pair shows 3 cups?
level2.explanation: Cups (x) come first, scoops (y) second. 3 cups need 3 × 2 = 6 scoops, so the point is (3, 6).
choiceFeedback: You doubled it, but check if that's the right scale factor.
Re-check how many times you need to multiply or scale.
This pairs 3 cups with 3 scoops, which would be 1 scoop per cup. Reread the recipe to see how many scoops a single cup needs.
level2.stemEs: Receta: 1 taza de bayas por 2 cucharadas de yogur. Con las tazas en x y las cucharadas en y, ¿cuál par muestra 3 tazas?
level2.explanationEs: Las tazas (x) van primero y las cucharadas (y) segundo. 3 tazas necesitan 3 × 2 = 6 cucharadas, así que el punto es (3, 6).
hints: On this graph the x-coordinate always stands for cups and the y-coordinate always stands for scoops.
Work out the scoops that go with 3 cups first, then write the pair with cups in front.
The recipe uses 2 scoops for every 1 cup, so 3 cups means 3 groups of 2 scoops. Find that total and put it second in the pair.
hintsEs: En esta gráfica, la coordenada x siempre representa las tazas y la coordenada y siempre representa las cucharadas.
Calcula primero las cucharadas que corresponden a 3 tazas y luego escribe el par con las tazas al frente.
La receta usa 2 cucharadas por cada 1 taza, así que 3 tazas son 3 grupos de 2 cucharadas. Halla ese total y colócalo en segundo lugar del par.

level2.stem: On the smoothie graph, every point follows the rule scoops = 2 × cups. Which equation describes the pattern between x (cups) and y (scoops)?
level2.explanation: Each cup needs 2 scoops, so y (scoops) is always 2 times x (cups): y = 2x. For 4 cups, y = 2 × 4 = 8.
choiceFeedback: Re-check how many times you need to multiply or scale.
Dividing would leave fewer scoops than cups. Check the recipe: does each cup call for more scoops or fewer?
The variables are flipped here, so this says cups are double the scoops. Make sure the scoops are what gets multiplied.
level2.stemEs: En la gráfica del batido, cada punto sigue la regla cucharadas = 2 × tazas. ¿Cuál ecuación describe el patrón entre x (tazas) y y (cucharadas)?
level2.explanationEs: Cada taza necesita 2 cucharadas, así que y (cucharadas) siempre es 2 veces x (tazas): y = 2x. Para 4 tazas, y = 2 × 4 = 8.
hints: An equation is just the rule of the ratio table rewritten with letters.
Decide which variable gets built from the other: the scoops depend on the cups, so y comes from x.
Test with numbers — 1 cup gives 2 scoops and 4 cups give 8 scoops. Which operation on x produces those y-values every time?
hintsEs: Una ecuación es solo la regla de la tabla de razones escrita con letras.
Decide cuál variable se construye a partir de la otra: las cucharadas dependen de las tazas, así que y sale de x.
Pruébalo con números: 1 taza da 2 cucharadas y 4 tazas dan 8 cucharadas. ¿Cuál operación sobre x produce esos valores de y siempre?

level2.stem: (Lesson 3.1) A fruit salad has 5 pieces of melon, 3 pieces of pineapple, and 2 grapes. What is the ratio of pineapple to melon?
level2.explanation: The ratio of pineapple to melon compares pineapple (3) to melon (5), so the ratio is 3:5.
choiceFeedback: The order matters — what is named first should be first in the ratio.
That compares pineapple to the total (5 + 3 + 2). The question compares pineapple to melon only.
You started with the pineapple, which fits the order — but 2 is the number of grapes. Re-read which two amounts the question compares.
hints: Three fruits are listed, but the question only compares pineapple and melon — the grapes are extra info.
Pick out just the two amounts you need, then write them in the order the question names: pineapple first.
Circle the pineapple count (3) and the melon count (5). Write them in the order 'pineapple to melon.'
level2.stemEs: Una ensalada de frutas tiene 5 trozos de melón, 3 trozos de piña y 2 uvas. ¿Cuál es la razón de piña a melón?
level2.explanationEs: La razón de piña a melón compara la piña (3) con el melón (5), así que la razón es 3:5.
hintsEs: Se mencionan tres frutas, pero la pregunta solo compara piña y melón — las uvas son información de más.
Escoge solo las dos cantidades que necesitas y escríbelas en el orden que nombra la pregunta: la piña primero.
Encierra la cantidad de piña (3) y la de melón (5). Escríbelas en el orden 'piña a melón'.

level3.stem: A student plots the points (1, 3), (2, 6), (3, 9), and (4, 15) from a ratio table. She says they form a straight line because they go up. Is she correct? Explain how to check.
level3.sampleAnswer: She is not correct. While the first three points follow the pattern y = 3x (3, 6, 9), the fourth point should be (4, 12), not (4, 15). If you plot all four points, (4, 15) would not land on the line through the others. The ratio 4:15 does not simplify to 1:3 like the others.
level3.hint: Remember to explain how the graph shows whether the points make the same ratio.
hints: 'They go up' isn't enough — a straight line needs every point to follow the SAME rule.
Find the rule from the first points (what do you multiply x by to get y?), then test every point against it — especially the last.
From (1, 3) the rule looks like y = 3 × x. Test (4, 15): multiply 4 × 3 and compare with 15. Explain what you find.
level3.stemEs: Una estudiante grafica los puntos (1, 3), (2, 6), (3, 9) y (4, 15) de una tabla de razones. Dice que forman una línea recta porque suben. ¿Tiene razón? Explica cómo comprobarlo.
level3.explanation: She is not correct. Rising is not enough — every point must give the same value of y ÷ x: 3÷1 = 3, 6÷2 = 3, and 9÷3 = 3, but 15÷4 = 3.75. To check, divide y by x at each point (or look for the same right-and-up step repeating), and (4, 15) sits above where the line would go.
level3.explanationEs: No tiene razón. Que suban no basta: cada punto debe dar el mismo valor de y ÷ x: 3÷1 = 3, 6÷2 = 3 y 9÷3 = 3, pero 15÷4 = 3.75. Para comprobarlo, divide y entre x en cada punto (o busca que se repita el mismo paso a la derecha y hacia arriba), y (4, 15) queda por encima de donde iría la línea.
hintsEs: 'Van subiendo' no basta: una recta necesita que cada punto siga la MISMA regla.
Halla la regla con los primeros puntos (¿por cuánto multiplicas x para obtener y?) y luego prueba cada punto, sobre todo el último.
Con (1, 3) la regla parece ser y = 3 × x. Prueba (4, 15): multiplica 4 × 3 y compara con 15. Explica lo que encuentres.

level3.stem: Recipe: 1 cup berries to 2 scoops yogurt. With cups on x and scoops on y, which pair shows 3 cups?
level3.explanation: Cups (x) come first, scoops (y) second. 3 cups need 3 × 2 = 6 scoops, so the point is (3, 6).
choiceFeedback: You doubled it, but check if that's the right scale factor.

level3.stemEs: Receta: 1 taza de bayas por 2 cucharadas de yogur. Con las tazas en x y las cucharadas en y, ¿cuál par muestra 3 tazas?
level3.explanationEs: Las tazas (x) van primero y las cucharadas (y) segundo. 3 tazas necesitan 3 × 2 = 6 cucharadas, así que el punto es (3, 6).
hints: On this graph the x-coordinate always stands for cups and the y-coordinate always stands for scoops.
Work out the scoops that go with 3 cups first, then write the pair with cups in front.
The recipe uses 2 scoops for every 1 cup, so 3 cups means 3 groups of 2 scoops. Find that total and put it second in the pair.
hintsEs: En esta gráfica, la coordenada x siempre representa las tazas y la coordenada y siempre representa las cucharadas.
Calcula primero las cucharadas que corresponden a 3 tazas y luego escribe el par con las tazas al frente.
La receta usa 2 cucharadas por cada 1 taza, así que 3 tazas son 3 grupos de 2 cucharadas. Halla ese total y colócalo en segundo lugar del par.

level3.stem: On the smoothie graph, every point follows the rule scoops = 2 × cups. Which equation describes the pattern between x (cups) and y (scoops)?
level3.explanation: Each cup needs 2 scoops, so y (scoops) is always 2 times x (cups): y = 2x. For 4 cups, y = 2 × 4 = 8.
choiceFeedback: Re-check how many times you need to multiply or scale.

level3.stemEs: En la gráfica del batido, cada punto sigue la regla cucharadas = 2 × tazas. ¿Cuál ecuación describe el patrón entre x (tazas) y y (cucharadas)?
level3.explanationEs: Cada taza necesita 2 cucharadas, así que y (cucharadas) siempre es 2 veces x (tazas): y = 2x. Para 4 tazas, y = 2 × 4 = 8.
hints: An equation is just the rule of the ratio table rewritten with letters.
Decide which variable gets built from the other: the scoops depend on the cups, so y comes from x.
Test with numbers — 1 cup gives 2 scoops and 4 cups give 8 scoops. Which operation on x produces those y-values every time?
hintsEs: Una ecuación es solo la regla de la tabla de razones escrita con letras.
Decide cuál variable se construye a partir de la otra: las cucharadas dependen de las tazas, así que y sale de x.
Pruébalo con números: 1 taza da 2 cucharadas y 4 tazas dan 8 cucharadas. ¿Cuál operación sobre x produce esos valores de y siempre?
